clue.text: Tyro who has lost his grip?

definitions.meaning: a tyro is a beginner or learner
read as ...: someone with ..., the bench tool that grips work

explanation.surface: A beginner who can no longer hold on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as 'no vice': a vice is the workshop clamp that grips, so a man without one has lost his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a raw beginner, a learner just starting out.

clue.text: Considering verdict on eccentric

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the verdict above the word for considering

parts.note: out is the umpire's verdict in cricket
re means concerning or considering

explanation.surface: Thinking over a judgment on someone odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional, bizarre.

clue.text: Dull single girl claiming to be a goddess

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Nan is a girl's name
a claim of 'I'm Ate', Ate being the Greek goddess of folly

explanation.surface: A boring unmarried girl who says she is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: The claim is 'I'm Ate': Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless, without spirit, hence dull.

clue.text: Boats for cruise, say

parts.note: racing shells that carry crews, 'cruise' heard as 'crews'

explanation.surface: Vessels suited to a pleasure trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruise, say' is 'crews' heard aloud: these rowing boats each carry a crew of oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing rowing boats each manned by a crew of oars plus cox are named for that crew size.

clue.text: Precision with which Bill takes position in church

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a curacy is the post held by a curate

explanation.surface: Asking how exactly a man named Bill got his church appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy and precision are synonyms: both mean exactness.

clue.text: Pick-me-ups in article on diet edited by newspaper workers

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: edited means altered, so the letters of diet are rearranged

parts.note: the press means newspapers
worker ants

explanation.surface: Tonics placed in a story about diets revised by journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Pills that lift the mood are informally called pick-me-ups.

clue.text: Fights swindle on nurses

indicators.note: on in a down clue sets the swindle above the word for nurses

parts.note: a con is a swindle
tends means nurses, looks after

explanation.surface: Battles over a fraud practised on hospital staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to struggle or compete.

clue.text: Might you meet an early one on the stairs?

definitions.text: Might you meet an early one on the stairs?

parts.words: Might you meet an early one on the stairs?
parts.note: the vertical part of each stair, and also a person who gets up at dawn

explanation.surface: Bumping into someone up at dawn on the staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright board of a step is so called, as is a person getting out of bed.

clue.text: Light meal in college at first rising

parts.note: COLL is an abbreviation for college

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word for first is read upwards

parts.note: No I, number one, means first

explanation.surface: A snack eaten in college at the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is NO I (number one); 'rising' turns it to ION after COLL and AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A collation is a light cold meal or snack.

clue.text: Tidy the ratings' mess up

indicators.note: to mess up is to throw into disorder, so the letters of the ratings are jumbled

explanation.surface: An order to clean up the sailors' dining quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess up' looks like naval slang for a ratings' mess hall, but signals that the letters of THE RATINGS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy something is to put it in order, set it right.

clue.text: Alone — therefore sounding depressed?

parts.note: so is a synonym of therefore

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for depressed is heard, not spelt

parts.note: low means depressed or downcast

explanation.surface: Being on your own, and so feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo performance is done by one person on their own.

clue.text: Shown to be a North Briton indeed

indicators.note: to be, with the clue read as 'in deed', places the Briton within the deed

parts.note: read as 'in deed': a deed is an act
the Picts were an ancient people of northern Britain

explanation.surface: Proof that someone really is a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'indeed' as 'in deed': the Pict sits in DEED, giving DE-PICT-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Depicted means portrayed, represented in a picture or account.

clue.text: Cerumen making organ grow more powerful

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
to wax is to increase, as the moon waxes

explanation.surface: Something that makes a bodily organ grow stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerumen is the medical name for the yellowish secretion in the ear canal.

clue.text: The fish is partly off, unfortunately

indicators.note: only a part of the word unfortunately is taken, the rest cut off

explanation.surface: Warning that the fish has gone a bit bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, often tinned.

clue.text: Fail to appreciate a French mistake in time

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in places the mistake inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Missing the worth of a French blunder made in time.
explanation.definitionFit: To underrate is to undervalue, judge too low.

clue.text: Initially, protein diet can turn out overexacting

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word protein
this word means the letters it governs are mixed up, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A high-protein diet can prove too demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' is the anagram signal on DIET CAN, giving EDANTIC after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over small details, so pedantic means fussy and overprecise.

clue.text: Wrought iron panel is a perfect example

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An ornamental ironwork panel held up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrought iron' seems a phrase, but 'Wrought' signals rearranging IRON PANEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonpareil is something without equal, a paragon.

clue.text: Top position for apprentice in boat

indicators.note: in sets the apprentice letter inside the boat

parts.note: a pinnace is a small ship's boat
L for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A senior post for a trainee aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner's letter, shown on British learner drivers' plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a peak, the highest point.

clue.text: Sidle like an owl — not face on

parts.note: to edge is to sidle, move sideways
owls are traditionally wise

explanation.surface: An owl creeping sideways rather than looking straight at you.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgewise means sideways, with the edge rather than the front turned forward.

clue.text: How right Penny's said to be!

definitions.text: How right Penny's said to be!

parts.words: How right Penny's said to be!
parts.note: the saying 'right as ... names a sum of pennies standing for being perfectly right

explanation.surface: Someone called Penny is reputed to be always correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'right as ninepence' means perfectly fine; the number of pence in it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepence is the coin sum in the saying used for being entirely right.

clue.text: Chesterton's man of mystery

parts.note: in G. K. Chesterton's 'Song Against ...' God made this shopkeeper 'for a mystery and a sign'

explanation.surface: A Father Brown-style detective by G. K. Chesterton.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterton wrote detective stories, so a sleuth seems meant; the line is from his poem mocking shopkeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's poem calls the food shopkeeper a wicked figure made for a mystery and a sign.

clue.text: It may be barred when the Prince's performing

parts.note: PR is an abbreviation for prince, and the 's stands for is
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A theatre shut whenever a certain Prince takes the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' suggests a banned show; it is the bars on cell windows.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail has bars on its windows and doors.

clue.text: Get well in this country

parts.note: a spa is a resort where people go to recover their health

explanation.surface: Recovering your health in a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a country of south-western Europe.

clue.text: Mountain pasture, almost running back to the sea

indicators.note: running back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse order

parts.note: Ossa is a mountain in Greece

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the word for pasture

parts.note: grass is pasture

explanation.surface: Upland grazing land sloping down to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: OSSA plus GRAS (grass, 'almost') read backwards gives the Sargasso Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sargasso is a sea in the North Atlantic, famous for floating seaweed.

clue.text: Unusually close to the foot of the column

indicators.note: unusually means out of the normal order, so the letters of close are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something oddly near the base of a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A socle is a plain plinth on which a column or statue stands.

clue.text: Sita's husband is fast losing a lion-tamer

indicators.note: losing tells us letters are removed from the word for fast

parts.note: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting
Dan, short for Daniel, survived the lions' den

explanation.surface: A Hindu heroine's husband loses a circus performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel was thrown into the lions' den and calmed them, hence the 'lion-tamer'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Ramayana, the god-king Rama is married to Sita.

clue.text: "Wherein I'll catch the — of the king" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "Wherein I'll catch the — of the king" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "Wherein I'll catch the — of the king" (Hamlet)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Hamlet's plan to stage a play that will expose Claudius's guilt

explanation.surface: A quotation from Hamlet with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'The play's the thing / Wherein I'll catch the — of the king'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet hopes the play will stir the king's inner moral sense and betray his guilt.

clue.text: Such enthusiasm needs a sharp head

parts.note: keen means sharp, as a blade
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Real eagerness requires a clear-thinking leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness is eagerness, zeal.

clue.text: Wave, or what produces one

definitions.meaning: a long heavy breaker on the sea
a hair curler puts a wave in hair

explanation.surface: A sea breaker, or the thing that makes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller is both a big breaking sea swell and a curler that sets a wave in hair.
